options.why: Cells accumulate in metaphase (57 compared with 12) and few reach anaphase, as expected if chromosomes cannot be pulled apart.

items.explanation_en:
The correct answer is The drug most likely interferes with spindle fibers, so cells stall in metaphase and do not complete anaphase.. Cells accumulate in metaphase (57 compared with 12) and few reach anaphase, as expected if chromosomes cannot be pulled apart.
The drug most likely blocks DNA replication, so cells cannot enter mitosis. is incorrect: Blocking replication would lower the number of cells entering mitosis, not increase the number in metaphase.
The drug most likely speeds up cytokinesis, so many cells are in telophase. is incorrect: The number of cells in telophase does not increase in the treated group.
The drug most likely has no effect on mitosis. is incorrect: The distribution of cells in the stages of mitosis changed.

difficulty.label: basic_learning
difficulty.rationale: Single small table with equal totals (400 each). The student only needs to compare columns and see that metaphase rises sharply while anaphase and telophase fall, which makes D the best description. Distractors are easy to reject: A (interphase count is only slightly lower in the treated group), B (the misconception that the presence of all stages means no effect), and C (the totals are both 400). It requires no calculation and no interpretation beyond describing the data, which is a skill 4.B entry-level task. Difficulty does not come from unfair sources.

difficulty.label: basic_learning
difficulty.rationale: Single-step quantitative item: read the control column, sum the four mitotic stages (64), divide by 400 to get 16%. The definition of mitotic index is given in the stem, so no outside knowledge is needed. Arithmetic is small and clean. Distractors target common slips (raw count, using interphase percent). There is little conceptual depth about cell cycle regulation, and the Treated column is unused for this question.

difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: Requires knowing mitotic index excludes interphase, summing mitotic stages from a table for two groups, computing two proportions, then a percent change. Distractors reflect realistic errors (treated index alone, percentage-point difference, ratio instead of change). Small integers, in-scope content, and clear wording make it typical full-mock difficulty rather than basic or advanced.

Distractors target straightforward misconceptions (blocked replication would raise interphase, faster cytokinesis would raise telophase, no effect contradicts the data). Only one concept and a short chain of reasoning are needed, so it is suitable for basic learning rather than a full mock.
